answer: Proof-of-burn registration resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to destroy native tokens to mint an identity. Filtering peers through this cryptographic prism blocks an adversarial plume of cloned bots. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of lost capital per registered identity, preventing the network from degrading into a porous karst of fake nodes. A key limitation is that deep-pocketed adversaries can simply absorb these burn costs to dominate consensus.
